title: Chenla
capsule: Chenla (Zhenla in Chinese sources; ចេនឡា in Khmer) is the designation used in Tang-dynasty annals for polities that succeeded Funan in mainland Southeast Asia, with the first independent ruler Bhavavarman I attested around 580 CE; his nephew Mahendravarman (Citrasena) is credited with conquering Funan by c. 616, and Isanavarman I (c. 616–635) founded the capital Isanapura and sent embassies to Sui China. After Jayavarman I (c. 657–681) the state fragmented into Land Chenla in the north and Water Chenla in the south, with Water Chenla subject to Javanese raids in the late eighth century. Jayavarman II unified the successor territories and in 802 performed a devaraja consecration on Phnom Kulen, founding the Khmer Empire and extinguishing the Chenla era.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Chenla's political history rests primarily on Chinese annals and a limited corpus of Old Khmer inscriptions; territorial boundaries are approximate reconstructions and debate continues over whether 'Chenla' denotes a unified polity or a loosely connected set of principalities.
